subject: BlueWave performance follow-up: context window constraints & next steps
messages:
From: Alicia Park <alicia@bluewave.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evan Liu <evan.liu@bluewave.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BlueWave kickoff / perf targets

Thanks for the call earlier — quick recap from our side and a couple of clarifying questions so your team can size a PoC. High-level goals: keep interactive query latency low for our analytics UX and support longer context for session history. Details below.

- Latency target: p95 <= 250ms for short responses (~<200 tokens).
- Streaming: for transcript-style outputs (3k-6k tokens) we need chunked streaming with first-token latency < 200ms and steady stream thereafter.
- Throughput & concurrency: expected steady-state 40 concurrent web sessions, peak 120 concurrent sessions during batch analysis windows. Typical query rate ~90 req/s, burst up to 250 req/s.
- Context: our session traces vary; typical input context is ~4k tokens, but in 10% of sessions we expect full history up to ~14k tokens. Outputs range 200-3k tokens depending on the use case.

As discussed, primary asks: can Redwood meet the p95 latency goal for short responses while still supporting the longer context cases via streaming or fallback behavior? Also please call out any tradeoffs we should expect (quantization, model variants, batching).

I've attached the call recording and a short spreadsheet with streaming example messages. Happy to walk through the doc on a follow-up.

Alicia Park
VP, Product
BlueWave Analytics

Attachment: call-recording-20260714.mp3 (audio)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Park <alicia@bluewave.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BlueWave performance follow-up: context window constraints & next steps

Thanks Alicia — great summary and helpful to have the spreadsheet. Below is a concise recap from our side plus concrete options so you can pick a path for the PoC.

Recap of requirements (my read):
- Interactive p95 target: <= 250ms for short responses (~<200 tokens).
- Streaming-first requirement for long outputs (3k+ tokens) with actionable first-token latency target <200ms.
- Concurrency: steady 40, peaks 120-250.
- Context envelope: common ~4k tokens, tail up to ~14k tokens in 10% of sessions.

Performance tradeoffs and options:
1) Low-latency prioritized (recommended for UX):
   - Restrict active context to ~6k tokens (session windowing + prefix caching).
   - Use a high-throughput model variant we can provision on Dedicated capacity (we can hit p95 <= 220ms for short responses at 40-80 concurrent sessions).
   - For long-history sessions, stream from a smaller summary model to rebuild context on-the-fly; fall back to non-streaming full-history path when necessary (higher latency).
   - Impact: fewer tokens sent into the LLM per request, better p95 but some truncation/summarization required.

2) Fuller context support (recommended if fidelity > latency):
   - Allow up to ~14k input tokens by switching to a model variant optimized for long-context on the backend (quantized config + larger GPU instance).
   - Expect p95 degradation for short responses (350-500ms range depending on concurrency) unless we provision more Dedicated capacity.
   - Streaming remains possible but will be constrained by kernel scheduling for very long prefix lengths.

3) Mixed policy (canary approach):
   - Default to option 1 for interactive sessions; promote specific enterprise users to option 2 based on feature flags.
   - This gives you the latency UX for most users while preserving full-history fidelity for power users.

Concrete next steps I propose: 
- Technical PoC: Redwood will stage a two-week PoC with two routes: low-latency config (6k window) and long-context config (14k window). We will provide a perf harness, sample ingestion scripts, and a streaming demo.
- Data needed from BlueWave: representative session traces (anonymized), a deck of 4-5 canonical flows you want to prioritize, and a spike window (date/time) we can replay.
- Logistics: Redwood will provide a short perf estimate and a sample config by end of day Thu. Can we schedule a 30-min kickoff Wed 7/21?

Attachment: streaming_requirements_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Ben and Marissa — can you add any sizing notes or risks below?

Best,
Jordan Blake
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Alicia Park <alicia@bluewave.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BlueWave performance follow-up: context window constraints & next steps

Jordan / Alicia — quick technical notes from the infra side (calling out risks and estimates).

Quoted from Jordan's recap:
> - Context envelope: common ~4k tokens, tail up to ~14k tokens in 10% of sessions.

Notes:
- Concurrency & throughput: to maintain p95 <= 250ms for short responses at ~90 req/s we recommend Dedicated pools with autoscale headroom for bursts. Shared hosted endpoints can get close but are riskier for predictable p95 under sustained bursts.
- Prefix/KV caching: prefix caching of session summaries reduces token work per request by ~30-60% in our experience. For BlueWave, a 6k active window with a prioritized prefix cache should handle the interactive target without extra GPUs.
- Streaming behavior: for very long outputs we stream from an incremental decode path — first-token can be fast if the active prefix is small; when decoding from full 14k prefix the first-token cost is dominated by KV cache warm-up and will add ~80-150ms at p95.
- Quantization/model variants: we can offer an int8 quantized long-context variant that reduces memory and increases throughput but may slightly affect output style in edge cases (we'll test during PoC).

Sizing estimate (very rough):
- Low-latency config (6k window): 2 x A100-equivalent pods with autoscale to 4 for burst -> targets p95 ~200ms at 100 req/s.
- Full-context config (14k window): 4 x A100-equivalent pods with autoscale to 8 -> targets p95 ~350ms at 100 req/s.

Action items I can own for PoC: provide perf_estimate_v1.pdf, set up canary routing, instrument tracing hooks for token-level latency.

Attachment: perf_estimate_v1.pdf (pdf)

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Alicia Park <alicia@bluewave.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Evan Liu <evan.liu@bluewave.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BlueWave performance follow-up: context window constraints & next steps

Thanks team — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. BlueWave is aligned with the mixed policy (option 3): prioritize low-latency by default and enable full-history routes for power users. A couple of clarifications and asks before kickoff: 

1) PoC scope: two-week window, we expect the perf harness to replay ~48 hours of representative traffic (we'll provide anonymized traces).
2) Success criteria: p95 <= 250ms for interactive flow (6k active window) across steady-state 40 concurrent sessions; streaming first-token <200ms for long outputs when using the summary+stream path.
3) Fallback behavior: if the system detects a 14k session it should either (a) trigger a canary long-context route, or (b) return a brief summary + offer a full generation async job. We prefer (a) for enterprise users.

Procurement: Evan and I will push the internal approval; I shared the DocuSign PO link in the related links. Let's lock the kickoff for Wed 21 Jul 10:00am PT — Jordan, Ben, Marissa available?

I'll send the anonymized traces today and invite the kickoff meeting.

Thanks — looking forward to the PoC.

Alicia Park
VP, Product
BlueWave Analytics
